measurements.prevalence_shift_note: within-eval prevalence falls 0.7442 (2018) -> 0.64 (2019) -> 0.4153 (2020), the measured COVID-era duration regime shift; per-issue-year figures are mandatory reading beside the pooled AUC; persistence holds Brier 0.22-0.36 across the shift; prevalence drift does not by itself determine AUC
measurements.headroom_finding: NO demonstrated headroom under this protocol. The runner-contract model (0.5068) trails the register-side site-persistence reference (0.6124) by 0.1056 AUC on identical eval rows - the same honest expectation recorded before the rebuild, now a measured finding. No paired model-vs-persistence interval was recomputed for the v2026.12 frame; on these same eval rows the v2026.10 per-row diagnostic (ns-bwa-diag-001, 19-column frame, model 0.5086) measured the analogous deficit at -0.1038 with row-level interval [-0.1693, -0.0357] and site-clustered interval [-0.1706, -0.0383], both excluding zero, and the v2026.12 observed gap is larger. The model sits at the calendar/identity control level (0.5075). This is a recorded defect, not an encouraging result: no figure from this artifact may be quoted without this comparison beside it. It does not prove every competent model must lose; it says the runner's own baseline does not demonstrate the task's discriminative claim above simple references.
